description.narrative:
Cancer is a growing public health threat in Africa, with incidence projected to nearly double by 2040. Yet young people—over 60% ofthe population—are underrepresented in prevention and policy. Europe and Africa share challenges in prevention, misinformation, andunequal access to care, making youth cooperation timely. The African Youth Cancer Ambassador Network will establish a joint Africa–Europe youth-led advocacy initiative training and connecting African and European young leaders to co-develop and implement evidence-based cancer prevention actions. Through online capacity-building, a joint Summer School, and cross-border working groups, participants will co-create policy recommendations, lead local outreach, and launch collaborative advocacy initiatives.
By linking African grassroots mobilisation with European policy advocacy experience, the project will produce a Youth Declaration on Cross-Continental Cancer Care and strengthen youth participation in cancer policy processes.
AFRYCAN will strengthen young people’s role as credible advocates and change agents for cancer prevention through three goals: (1) train and mobilise 50 African and 15 European youth leaders with practical skills to design, deliver and communicate evidence-based prevention actions; (2) increase youth influence on prevention and early detection policy by equipping ambassadors to engage decision-makers on key risk factors, screening and equitable access; and (3) build sustained Africa–Europe cooperation in cancer advocacy through joint learning and coordinated action.
Implementation starts with online capacity-building and mentoring, followed by a joint Summer School to launch the first cohort, agree networkpriorities, and set up a digital Knowledge Hub for resources and collaboration.
Expected impact: 65 trained youth leaders with hands-on advocacy experience; at least five national and one regional youth-led policy dialogues initiated; at least five cross-border advocacy initiatives implemented; and higher public awareness of prevention and early detection, reducing stigma and misinformation.These results will strengthen youth participation in cancer policy and sustain cooperation beyond the grant period.

participating-org.narrative:
The Africa Public Health Student Network Initiative (AfricaPHSN) is a youth-led organization founded in 2022 that connects African students and young professionals in medical and health sciences who have a strong interest in public health. The organization works to strengthen Africa’s health systems through education, advocacy, research, and community-driven initiatives, with particular attention to climate-sensitive health issues and sustainable practices.
Vision: AfricaPHSN envisions a safer and healthier Africa where all people have access to the highest quality health services, promoting equity and strong, resilient health systems across the continent.
Mission: The mission of AfricaPHSN is to advance public health in Africa by promoting access to quality services for the timely prevention, detection, and response to public health threats through evidence-based programs and interventions.
Objectives: AfricaPHSN aims to provide pre-service education and capacity building for future healthcare providers, foster youth-led innovation in public health, support advocacy and research, and contribute to the development of resilient and context-appropriate health infrastructure. The organization prioritizes workforce development, disease prevention, emergency preparedness, and policy innovation.
Values: Core values are African-led (addressing local priorities), innovation, accountability (via partnerships), integrity (ethical standards), collaboration (forging partnerships), excellence (results-driven services), and impact (evidence-based outcomes). These guide their commitment to equitable and sustainable public health efforts.
